history.period: Early 20th century (Rameshwar Singh's reign, 1898-1929; exact year not published)
history.summary: White-marble Hanuman temple in Kathalbari on the Darbhanga Raj campus, near the Kameshwar Singh Darbhanga Sanskrit University. Local accounts say it was built by Maharaja Rameshwar Singh for a shorter-statured relative: the shrine stands on a raised platform about seven feet high with a low entrance, so devotees bow humbly as they approach the idol. Its famous tradition is wish-writing - devotees write their wishes directly on the temple walls, believing Hanuman will fulfil them; laddoos are the customary offering. NOTE: the foundation story rests on blog/travel sources; no authoritative construction date or inscriptional record is published. Coordinates are locality-level (Kathalbari area), not a verified POI match.

name: Manokamna Temple, Darbhanga
town_description: Darbhanga is a major city in north Bihar's Mithila region and the former seat of the Darbhanga Raj, whose palaces, forts, temples and ponds (such as Harahi and Dighi) dot the city. It hosts Lalit Narain Mithila University and Kameshwar Singh Darbhanga Sanskrit University, and its many Kali and Durga temples - including the famous Shyama Mai temple - make it a noted centre of Shakti worship.
